n2254.source: tr. Herbert Weir Smyth, New York 1922 (Perseus)
lines: which inhabit the tomb; and you, Zeus the Savior, invoked third, the guardian of the habitations of righteous men: receive as suppliants this band of women with the compassionate spirit of the land. But

n2254.source: tr. Herbert Weir Smyth, New York 1922 (Perseus)
lines: Stronger than a castle is an altar—an impenetrable shield. As quick as you can, gather in your left hands your white-wreathed suppliant boughs, sacred emblems of Zeus the merciful.

n2254.source: tr. Herbert Weir Smyth, New York 1922 (Perseus)
lines: Hear now the end of my appeals for compassion.
